newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. inquiry cannot explain Cyprus shooting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. inquiry cannot explain Cyprus shooting.

text.p: United Nations forces in Cyprus on Saturday said they were unable to find any evidence to explain a reported shooting incident near the dividing line between Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.
The Turkish Cypriot administration had said that shooting broke out early on Thursday when Greek Cypriots tried to take down the Turkish Cypriot flag north of the buffer zone.

The Greek Cypriot-led Cyprus government, which controls the southern part of the island, had denied the army was involved in any incident and said police had no information of civilian injuries or suspicious movements in the area.

"UNFICYP thoroughly searched the buffer zone in the area concerned, both on the ground and from the air, and did not find anything which could shed further light on the matter," the U.N. peacekeeping force said in a statement.

The U.N. force, which launched an inquiry after the reported incident, was beefed up in the area where the shots were heard, the statement said. The incident took place in the vicinity of the Turkish-held village of Louroujina, 20 km (12 miles) southeast of Nicosia.
U.N. spokesman Waldemar Rokosewski had said the force had initial information shots were fired by both sides, but later clarified that this was according to claims made by the Turkish military.

U.N. troops stationed on Cyprus patrol a buffer zone that has separated the two communities since Turkey invaded Cyprus's north in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then in power in Greece.
Tensions in Cyprus were fanned last month by a row over Greek Cypriot plans to deploy anti-aircraft missiles.
